clue.text: Central character is removed from well-liked tree

indicators.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter synonym is taken out, leaving the rest closed up

parts.note: someone well-liked is popular

explanation.surface: A storyteller's lead figure has been cut from a beloved piece of writing about a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central character' sounds like a hero in a story; here it is the middle letter, U, of the seven-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing species of tree, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Young attendant annually emptied greenhouse

parts.note: PA is short for per annum, Latin for annually

indicators.note: emptied means its inside letters are removed, leaving only the first and last

explanation.surface: A boy helper clears out the greenhouse once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a boy who attends a bride or, historically, serves a noble, so a young attendant.

clue.text: Greek character joins American returning on musical instrument

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word on is read backwards

explanation.surface: A Greek joins an American who is coming back to play an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The piano is a keyboard instrument with hammers striking strings, a member of the category.

clue.text: Type of band originates somewhere in mid-Australia

parts.note: an Alice band is a wide hairband, named after Alice in Wonderland's illustrations
springs means arises or originates

explanation.surface: A style of music group begins out in the Australian outback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians; it is a hairband, the Alice band, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a town in the Northern Territory near the geographical centre of Australia.

clue.text: Crazy about eastern honey-based drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for crazy goes round the letter for eastern

parts.note: crazy means mad

explanation.surface: Someone is wildly keen on an eastern drink made with honey.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an old fermented drink made from honey and water, which is exactly what the definition describes.

clue.text: Divorcee quietly learning to make a thorough investigation

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, such as a divorcee
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
lore is learning or traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A divorced person quietly studies in order to dig deep into some subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore is to examine or investigate something thoroughly, a direct synonym of the definition phrase.

clue.text: Debate is moving about illness

indicators.note: moving about means the letters shift position, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A discussion is circulating concerning a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabetes is a chronic disease affecting blood sugar regulation, an example of an illness.

clue.text: Pieces of information, whichever way you look

definitions.note: the definition phrase supplies the word itself, a short form of statistics, which the indicator then says is a palindrome

indicators.note: the letters read the same forwards and backwards, so the answer is a palindrome

parts.note: the definition phrase supplies the word itself, a short form of statistics, which the indicator then says is a palindrome

explanation.surface: Data that holds wherever you turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alone gives the word; the rest says it reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Stats is informal shorthand for statistics, numerical facts or data.

clue.text: Flatten incisive article perhaps taken out of newspaper

definitions.text: article perhaps taken out of newspaper

parts.note: to press something is to flatten it
a cutting remark is sharp and incisive

explanation.surface: A sharp piece of writing is squashed after being clipped from a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A press cutting is an item clipped from a newspaper or magazine, typically an article.

clue.text: Combatant pleased with schedule one brought over

parts.note: pleased means glad

indicators.note: brought over means turned over, so the schedule word and the numeral one are read backwards together

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fighter is happy with a timetable that someone has delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' reverses the schedule word and the numeral together, so the I lands before the turned-round letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a fighter in Roman arenas, so a combatant by trade.

clue.text: Initially pick each vegetable

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice to start by choosing every vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is a small green seed eaten as a common vegetable, an example of the category.

clue.text: Ancient piece of rock, relocated at store, fourteen pounds

indicators.note: relocated means moved to new positions, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: a stone is a British unit of weight equal to fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: An old chunk of rock has been moved to a shop, and it weighs fourteen pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocated' rearranges AT STORE to give ROSETTA. A stone is a British weight still used for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rosetta Stone is an ancient inscribed granodiorite slab, the key to deciphering Egyptian hieroglyphs, so literally an old piece of rock.

clue.text: Couple allowed jewellery

parts.note: a brace is a pair or couple, as of game birds
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A pair were permitted to wear jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn on the wrist, an example of jewellery.

clue.text: Around back of library, Peter arranged to use keyboard again

indicators.note: around means placed about, so the rearranged name goes round the single letter
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of the name are shuffled
back of means the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Peter, near the rear of a library, sorts things out so he can key text in once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns PETER into RETPE; 'Around' puts it around Y, the last letter of 'library'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype is to key text in a second time on a keyboard, exactly the definition's action.

clue.text: Brown, curiously dark drinking vessel

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters of the word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A brown, oddly dark mug for drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large beer mug, often pewter with a handle, a vessel for drinking.

clue.text: Plan section of Porsche meticulously

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Design work on part of a Porsche carried out with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a plan or systematic arrangement for doing something; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: The man will start to offer greeting

parts.note: he refers to a man
'll is the contracted form of will

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A man is going to begin offering a welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the standard word said when meeting someone, a common greeting.

clue.text: Private trick female recreated in detail

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

indicators.note: recreated means made again in a new form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier's deception, a woman reconstructed with every detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreated' signals the anagram. 'Private' looks like a soldier but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confidential is kept secret and not for the public, so private in the adjective sense.

clue.text: Unique beer catches on

indicators.note: catches means holds within, so the beer word goes round the other word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind beer becomes popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches on' reads as becoming popular, but 'on' is the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone can mean unique or unequalled, as in 'she stands alone among singers'.

clue.text: Motor-bike meeting outside in shade

indicators.note: outside means around, so the race abbreviation encloses the following word

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race meeting on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A motorcycle rally gathers outdoors in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is an annual motorbike road race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a shade or slight variety of a colour.

clue.text: Open meadow clear when boundaries gone

indicators.note: boundaries are the outer edges, so the word's first and last letters are dropped, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A meadow becomes open ground once the fences are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic or old word for an open grassy field or pasture.

clue.text: World War 1 battle, first two leaving Libyan capital after bitterness

indicators.note: after says the trimmed capital follows the word for bitterness

parts.note: gall means bitterness or rancour

indicators.note: the first two letters of the city's name are removed

parts.note: Tripoli is the capital of Libya

explanation.surface: A First World War battle where two leading figures quit the Libyan capital with resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first two leaving' drops TR from TRIPOLI, giving IPOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli was the 1915-16 Allied campaign against the Ottomans on the Dardanelles peninsula, a famous battle of the Great War.

clue.text: Commotion also restricts daughter

indicators.note: restricts means hems in, so the word for also encloses the letter for daughter

parts.note: also means too

explanation.surface: A fuss also keeps a daughter confined.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion; the two are synonyms in informal English.

clue.text: Old English king, for example, right to interrupt little Elizabeth

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into, so the letter for right goes inside the pet name

parts.note: Bet is a short pet form of the name Elizabeth

explanation.surface: An old English monarch, say, has a right to break in on young Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Egbert was a ninth-century king of Wessex, often called the first king of all England, so an early English ruler.
